title: Registry pinning + routing compatibility matrix notes
content:
Purpose and scope:

Quick working notes on interactions between the Model Registry (version pinning) and routing policies in the control plane across multi-region deployments. Intent: capture compatibility constraints, failure/fallback semantics, and a proposed minimal validation + routing algorithm to avoid serving incompatible model/runtime combinations. This is an engineering-first doc — rough, prioritized for clarity over polish.

Context / motivation:
- Customers can pin a model version (e.g., customer:my-model@v2.1) in route configs and expect deterministic outputs.
- The control plane routes requests by policy (latency-first, cost-first, region-affinity, tiered fallbacks).
- We support model variants (float32 / int8-quant / gqa) and runtime variants (gpu-optimized, cpu-fallback, low-memory kernels). Some combinations are incompatible (e.g., quantized checkpoint not supported on legacy kernel).
- When capacity is constrained or a region outage occurs, routing may need to fall back to a compatible model variant or to a different region. Pinning semantics must be honored or explicit degradation behavior applied.

Goals:
1) Define a compatibility matrix between model artifacts, runtime/kernels, and quantization formats.
2) Describe how version pinning influences routing decisions and allowed fallbacks.
3) Propose control-plane validation checks to reject unsafe route configs at creation time.
4) Provide pseudocode for routing decisions that balance pinning guarantees, SLOs, and availability.

Assumptions:
- Model registry metadata includes: model_id, version, supported_kernels[], required_kv_schema, quant_formats[], max_sequence_len, kv_cache_schema_version.
- Runtime nodes expose capabilities: kernel_set[], quant_support[], max_seq_len, region, instance_type, capacity_score.
- Pinning can be either strict (exact version) or loose (major/minor ranges). Routes indicate pinning_mode: strict | semver_range | latest-compatible.
- Customers may opt-in to 'allow_region_fallback' and 'allow_model_variant_fallback' booleans per route. Default: allow_model_variant_fallback=false, allow_region_fallback=true.

Definitions / compatibility dimensions:
- Kernel compatibility: kernel A supports model ops X, Y. Some kernels compiled for specific attention types cannot run models that use fused ops.
- Quantization compatibility: a quantized checkpoint has quant_format tags (e.g., int8-gptq, int4-adaptive). Runtimes must advertise support for those formats.
- KV cache schema: model may require KV schema v2; older runtime kernels only support v1.
- IO contract: tokenizer + streaming hooks; model must declare streaming_enabled true/false.

Compatibility matrix (example, ASCII):

Columns: model-version | quant_formats | kv_schema | required_kernels | notes
--------------------------------------------------------------
my-model@v2.0 | float32 | v1 | kernel-A,kernel-B | legacy v2.0, no streaming
my-model@v2.1 | int8-gptq,float32 | v2 | kernel-B,kernel-C | prefers kernel-C for performance
my-model@v3.0 | int4-adaptive | v2 | kernel-C | requires kv_schema v2, streaming=true

Runtime capability samples:
runtime-X (region-us-east) -> kernels: kernel-A,kernel-B | quants: float32,int8-gptq | kv:v1 | capacity: 1200
runtime-Y (region-eu-west) -> kernels: kernel-B,kernel-C | quants: float32,int8-gptq,int4-adaptive | kv:v2 | capacity: 800

Compatibility conclusions:
- v2.1 can run on runtime-X and runtime-Y, but runtime-X will provide degraded behavior for features that need kv:v2 (if any). If kv_schema mismatch -> must disallow or emulate with cache-miss penalty.
- v3.0 cannot run on runtime-X because runtime-X lacks int4 support and kv:v2.

Routing + pinning semantics:
- strict pinning: request must be routed to a node that can run exactly that model-version artifact using its declared requirements. No variant or region substitution allowed unless customer explicitly opts in to an "emergency-fallback" policy.
- semver_range pinning: route allows any version within the specified semver range, but the control plane must prefer the highest compatible version that satisfies kernel/quant constraints for the chosen runtime.
- latest-compatible: control plane may choose any newer version if it is compatible; must respect opt-out flags for breaking changes (e.g., kv schema bump).

Fallback types and priority (when pinning allows fallbacks):
1) Model variant fallback (e.g., float32 -> int8 if model provides a quantized artifact and runtime supports int8) when 'allow_model_variant_fallback' true. Prefer variants in order: exact-quant-match -> highest-accuracy supported -> fastest.
2) Region fallback: if the local region has no compatible capacity, route to next region according to geo-policy and latency budget, only if 'allow_region_fallback' true.
3) Runtime downgrade: route to a runtime with lower instance_type but compatible kernels, only if latency SLO allows.

Control plane validation and checks (route create / update):
- On route creation with pinned_version V and pinning_mode M: validate registry[model:V].required_kernels intersects available_global_kernels. If strict pin and intersection empty -> reject route with message listing required kernels and suggested runtime types.
- If route allows variant fallback, ensure registry lists at least one alternate artifact (quantized or other) and annotate route with fallback candidates.
- If route uses semver_range, enumerate candidate versions and compute the union of required features; flag if any candidate introduces incompatible kv_schema bump unless the route explicitly allows schema migration.
- For multi-region pinned routes, annotate per-region compatibility and mark regions as 'incompatible' to prevent routing there. Provide a per-route region compatibility report stored as route metadata.

Routing decision pseudocode (simplified):

function choose_node(request, route_config):
  candidates = nodes_in_scope(route_config) // region filter, tenant isolation
  if route_config.pinning_mode == 'strict':
    candidates = candidates.filter(node => node.can_run(route_config.pinned_version))
    if candidates.empty and not route_config.allow_emergency_fallback:
      return error("No compatible capacity for pinned version")
    if candidates.empty and route_config.allow_emergency_fallback:
      candidates = candidates.filter(node => node.can_run_any_variant(route_config.model_id))
  else if pinning_mode == 'semver_range' or 'latest-compatible':
    version = select_preferred_version(route_config, candidates)
    candidates = candidates.filter(node => node.can_run(version))

  // scoring: prefer same-region, then latency_score, then cost_score
  scored = score_candidates(candidates, request.slo, route_config.policy_weights)
  return pick_top(scored)

Notes on scoring: include a penalty for cross-region routing that grows with request.latency_budget; include a large penalty for switching quant format away from the model-author recommended format unless allowed by route flags.

Multi-region considerations and eventual consistency:
- Registry updates (new model versions) are propagated asynchronously. When a route pins to 'latest-compatible', there is a window where control plane snapshots may disagree across regions. Mitigation: include a versioned 'compatibility snapshot' timestamp included in route metadata; any routing decision must reference the snapshot epoch when evaluating compatibility.
- Rollouts: when performing canary rollouts of new model version, update registry with rollout tags and mark only a subset of nodes as allowed. The routing layer must consult rollout tags and percentage buckets to ensure proper traffic steering. Pinning semantics: customers pinning 'strict' should not be moved into canary traffic unless they deliberately request the new version.

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Kernel ABI change: new kernel introduces same name but different ABI -> registry must include kernel_abi_version and routing must validate kernel_abi_version equality.
- KV schema mismatch: if runtime can emulate older kv schema via shim, add a runtime flag 'kv_emulation:true' and quantize the expected perf degradation in the compatibility report.
- Tokenizer mismatch: model registry must record tokenizer_hash. If runtime exposes a different tokenizer, flag incompatibility unless 'allow_tokenizer_override' true and a mapping exists.

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests: matrix-driven tests that enumerate combinations of model versions, runtime capabilities, and route flags. Expect deterministic accept/reject decisions.
- Integration: simulate region outage and verify pinned-strict routes fail with clear error; pinned-loose routes successfully fallback according to policy.
- Chaos: fuzz registry propagation delays and ensure routing honors compatibility snapshot epochs.

Migration / rollout plan for enforcement:
1) Start with advisory mode: new route creation prints compatibility warnings but allows creation. Export a per-route compatibility report in Console API.
2) After 4 weeks of warnings and opt-ins, flip validation to block invalid strict-pinned routes.
3) Add UI in Console to present per-region compatibility and suggested remediation (e.g., build quantized artifact, enable kv_emulation).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define a canonical scoring function and expose weights to orgs (how much to prefer cost vs pinned-version correctness).
- Should we allow automated on-the-fly model transforms (e.g., auto-quantize float32 -> int8) as an emergency fallback? (privacy and perf implications).
- How to surface the compatibility snapshot epoch to customers for debugging? Add header X-Redwood-Compat-Epoch?
- Need a small language in docs and SLA that clarifies customer expectations for strict pinning during region outages.

Action items (owners):
- (Priya) prototype compatibility-check library for registry -> runtime intersection (due 2024-10-01).
- (Ethan) create matrix-driven unit tests and include example datasets (due 2024-10-10).
- (Marta) add console UI mockups for per-route compatibility (due 2024-10-15).
- (Samir) draft SLA blurb and API header proposal for compat-epoch (due 2024-10-05).

Notes to self:
- Keep the strict semantics conservative by default. Customers who want aggressive fallbacks can enable opt-ins; make them explicit.
- Compatibility reports should be cheap to compute (cached per registry publish) and small enough to surface in route creation APIs.

References / links: registry spec draft (CONFLUENCE-4567), routing policy design doc (JIRA-INFR-1023), runtime kernel catalog PR (github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pulls/189).

End of notes.
